tagline: Across Dixville Notch and along the Androscoggin through moose country
intro: The Moose Path Trail crosses Dixville Notch and follows the Androscoggin through the 13 Mile Woods Scenic Area. NH 26 passes through a short, steep-walled gorge dividing the Connecticut and Androscoggin watersheds. Visit NH presents the byway as a drive for wildlife viewing and woodland heritage. Moose are often seen in low, swampy ground beside the road. The notch has waterfalls on two mountain brooks.

An earlier route through the notch served a winter trade. After the Coos Trail opened in 1803, farmers hauled wheat, potash and other produce by sled to Portland, exchanging them for molasses, saltfish and necessities. Route 26 now follows the old trail through Dixville Notch. Farther south, the Androscoggin carried timber to paper mills in Berlin. Pontook Dam was reconstructed in the mid-1980s for hydroelectric generation; Dummer’s reservoir also became a destination for canoeists, kayakers and birdwatchers.

Traveling south from Pittsburg, US 3 leads through West Stewartstown to Colebrook. There NH 26 heads east through Dixville Notch to Errol. Turn south on NH 16 for the river corridor through 13 Mile Woods and Pontook Reservoir, then Dummer, Milan and Berlin. The drive reaches Gorham, where NH 16 meets US 2 beside the Androscoggin.

moments.title: Dixville Notch
moments.text: Dixville Notch’s midnight voting began with the 1960 election. Neil Tillotson, who owned The Balsams, disliked the 45-minute drive to the nearest polling station and learned of midnight voting from an Associated Press reporter. The state legislature approved a voting precinct for the community. Residents gather at midnight for presidential primary and general elections; the polls close once every registered voter has voted. In 1964, UPI and the Associated Press reported its primary returns first in New Hampshire. The village sits at about 1,800 feet above sea level, below the mountain pass that shares its name.

moments.title: Dixville Notch State Park
moments.text: Two mountain brooks carry waterfalls through Dixville Notch State Park, where NH 26 crosses the mountain gap. The park covers 127 acres, and trails climb toward the summits of nearby mountains. The short, steep-walled gorge marks the divide between the Connecticut and Androscoggin river systems. Travelers were staying beside the notch by 1866, when George Parsons established the Dix House on Lake Gloriette’s shore, just west of the pass. Three decades later, Henry Hale bought the site and built The Balsams there. The park lies in Dixville Township, with Route 26 running through the notch itself.
moments.notice: Waterfalls run on two mountain brooks within the park.

moments.title: Pontook Reservoir
moments.text: Pontook Reservoir spreads over 379 acres of the Androscoggin River in Dummer. The river once carried log drives to Berlin’s paper mills downstream. Pontook Dam was reconstructed in the mid-1980s to generate hydroelectric power. The impounded water also draws canoeists, kayakers and birdwatchers. Below the dam are class III rapids.
